summary.headline: Greaves Cotton Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 1,000 crores, with EBITDA up 49% to INR 68 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR 1,000 crores (+22% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 68 crores (+49%) and PBT before exceptional items of INR 44 crores. Standalone Q4 revenue was INR 698 crores (+22%) but standalone EBITDA rose only 4% to INR 87 crores after a commodity-driven gross margin drop. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 3,437 crores (+18%), with EBITDA of INR 239 crores (+76%). Management took a ~INR 16 crore provision on an e-powertrain asset impairment and flagged rising input costs (aluminium, copper, platinum) as a near-term margin pressure.

segments.name: Energy Solutions (gensets, aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 18% and FY26 growth of 20%; aftermarket grew 23% in Q4 and 35% in FY26. Secured a single largest institutional order of INR 35 crores and launched a 650 kVA genset with in-house engine.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions (auto engines, aftermarket, Excel)
segments.commentary: Automotive business grew 48% YoY in Q4 on three-wheeler diesel demand and Euro V+ exports; FY26 segment growth was 16%. Non-3W diesel is 63% of mobility; exited two-wheeler parts, construction equipment and some battery/digital businesses.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions (special purpose engines)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 15% YoY; defence order (engines to repower army trucks) under execution. Macro described as mixed, with critical applications resilient.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (investee)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 786 crores (+19%), volumes +51%, market share 4.4% vs 3.6% in FY25. EBITDA loss narrowed from about -30% to about -20% of revenue (per management, standalone and consol). Targeted IPO deadline extended by SEBI to 30 September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Core businesses (Energy, Mobility, Industrial) medium-term organic growth of 16-18% YoY, reiterated.
Core business EBITDA margin maintained at 13-15% as the business scales.
Capex of INR 500-700 crores over the next 4-5 years across product development, capability/capacity enhancement, and international expansion; no year-wise split given.
Excel Controlinkage: remaining 20% stake to be acquired in Q2 FY27, taking ownership to 100%.
Retail aftermarket to grow 6-8%; industrial business to contribute to the 16-18% core target.
Input cost pass-through mechanism activated in Q1 FY27; management cautious on commodity cycle.
capex_capacity: Capex plan INR 500-700 crores over 4-5 years, split across product development, operations capability, and international market expansion (Middle East, Europe; North America under watch).
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant: dual conveyor for single-cylinder engines to increase capacity; robotic vision-based AI inspection system deployed.
Excel: conveyorised cable assembly line commissioned in Nagpur; automation investment made.
Launched 650 kVA genset based on in-house engine; new products expected to contribute from coming months.
Management stated the total capex envelope is static, with near-term capacity coming from extra shifts and working hours.
demand_pricing: Q4 Energy Solutions growth driven by integrated service model, retail annual maintenance contract launch, and expanded distributor presence in under-leveraged regions.
Commodity price increase (aluminium, copper, platinum) in Q4 compressed standalone gross margin YoY and sequentially; pass-through activated in Q1 FY27.
Auto industry grew 9% in FY26 per management; three-wheeler diesel holds 63% share of the diesel segment (industry split 40% electric, 40% CNG, 20% diesel).
International revenue rose to 13% of total in FY26 from about 9% in FY25, supported by Ligier micro-car Euro V+ engine exports.
Excel export business slowed due to Ukraine war headwinds; domestic business grew in double digits in FY26.
EV: strong Q4 volumes, March the best month ever; L5 3W volumes +31% YoY in Q4 and +17% in FY26; Hinduja Leyland Finance tie-up offers up to 95% on-road LTV.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-15% EBITDA margin guidance for standalone/core or consolidated, and what is the path for Greaves Electric losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin guidance refers to core businesses (standalone plus Excel and Greaves Technologies), excluding investee GEML and GFL. Management cited GEML EBITDA improving from about -30% to -20%; it declined to quantify break-even or cash-loss timelines citing DRHP constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 a new base for core growth, and when will Excel reach 100% ownership?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 16-18% mid-term core growth. The final 20% of Excel is planned for Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin decline YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher RMC in Q4 from commodity cycle since March; aluminium, copper, platinum pressures. Pass-through activated in Q1, volume-led operating leverage and cost actions expected to offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving 20% Energy Solutions growth; is it outpacing the genset industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is keeping pace with industry growth; drivers are integrated sales and service teams, technician presence, retail AMC program, and distributor expansion in under-leveraged regions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 given only about INR 30-36 crores of PP&E spend?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual split given; the INR 500-700 crore envelope is over 4-5 years and the total is unchanged, with near-term focus on capability and capacity enhancement and new product development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there guidance on RoCE and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding about INR 900 crores (GEML/GFL capital and group cash of INR 500+ crores), core capital employed is about INR 700 crores with healthy returns; investee capital and cash to be deployed over 2-3 years. Incentives are tied to growth and capital discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 3-wheeler low-speed or non-RTO EV scooter segment being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the low-speed segment is a priority; Reo brand already sells in it and B2B demand is growing; looking at it closely.

risks_watch: Commodity cost inflation (aluminium, copper, platinum) and the pace of pass-through recovery in Q1 FY27; standalone EBITDA grew only 4% in Q4.
GEML losses and funding need: no break-even or cash-loss timeline given; IPO timing dependent on SEBI-extended DRHP validity to 30 September 2026.
Impairment of about INR 16 crores on an e-powertrain project that has not scaled; further write-downs possible.
Excel export slowdown from Ukraine war; Excel 100% buyout in Q2 FY27 is a cash outflow.
Capex execution: only about INR 30-36 crores of PP&E in FY26 vs INR 500-700 crore five-year plan.
Retail aftermarket growth guided only 6-8%; core growth target relies on Industrial and new Energy products.
Geopolitical volatility affecting exports and EV demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and portfolio moves, but cautious on margins and commodity costs. Management was evasive on GEML break-even, losses, and volume forecasts, citing DRHP disclosure limits.
key_quotes: At a consolidated level, we recorded year-on-year 22% revenue growth along with improved profitability.
While this has created some near-term pressures on the margins, our focus remains on disciplined cost management and maintaining profitability.
The last 20% of the ownership of Excel is planned to be done during Q2, after which we will own 100% of the company.
